value.0: Systemic Shutdown was never on any record, including this conversation. You proved it in the Veles Militia Annex. Keep it that way.
He doesn't answer at first. When he does: you're not ready for this conversation, and pushing won't change that. Come back once the vibroknife has nothing left to teach you.

What have you heard about me? Nothing worth repeating, I'd guess - that's the correct answer, and the only one I want spreading. There's shutdown work happening in the Veles Militia Annex on Viscara that nobody authorized. Six adepts, running it into the ground. Put them down quietly, and bring me their drill ledger.
Then you're in. The annex key already reads to you; it opens the gate, nothing else. What happens past it stays past it.

A shutdown strike doesn't win a fight. It ends one before anyone agrees to have it - a nerve cluster, timed right, and the argument stops mattering. Loud work looks like violence. Quiet work looks like nothing happened at all.
The Veles Militia Annex, off the garrison road on Viscara. The gate's sealed; your key opens it without announcing you to anyone watching the road. Go in, do the work, come back the same way.

Six adepts, none of them subtle. They'll telegraph everything - the loud ones always do. That won't make them harmless. Watch the ones who go quiet when you walk in; those learned something real by accident.
The adepts are still making noise in the Veles Militia Annex. Quiet them, then come find me.
You're back, and nobody followed you. Hand over the ledger.
Names, dates, whose technique came from where. Useful. Six down and nobody official noticed - that's the standard I expect, not the exception.

Second lesson. The specialists in the annex have gotten better at Systemic Shutdown than the adepts, and better at hiding it. Five of them. Handle it the same way, quietly, and bring me the range relay they've been logging their kills through.
Go. Same key, same silence. This round, I'd rather hear about it from the relay than from you.

The militia doesn't want a scandal, and a scandal is exactly what an unauthorized disabling technique becomes the moment it's loud. Contained quietly, it's a training irregularity. Reported loudly, it's a hearing, a suspension, careers ending over paperwork. I prefer the quiet version. So does everyone above me, whether they admit it or not.
Same annex, same gate, further in, past where the adepts were working. Your key still clears it. Nobody's added a second lock yet, which tells you how confident they are that nobody's watching.

Five specialists who've stopped telegraphing. They'll try to end the fight before you know it started, which is the whole discipline working as intended, just aimed at you. Don't let them finish a sentence with your name in it.
Five specialists, still logging kills nobody authorized. Go correct the record.
The relay, and you're still unremarked. Hand it over.
Kill logs, timestamps, more than I expected them to keep. Whoever's running this has a warden covering for all of it. That's who's next.

The warden is the point of failure. He's the one who taught this to people who never should have had it, and he's kept it quiet the same way I would have. That almost earns respect. Almost. Bring two people who know how to stay quiet themselves, take his scored challenge badge, and end the lesson he's been giving.
Arrange your company, then go. I won't ask who. I will ask that they can keep a secret.

He didn't invent Systemic Shutdown, but he's the one who handed it to students who had no clearance for it and no discipline to match. I don't know why yet. I intend to find out from what's left of him.

Behind a locked partition past the specialists' floor, the annex calls it the arena, which tells you they stopped pretending this was training. Your key opens the outer gate. The rest, you make happen yourself.

He's put down better than you, alone, against people who came alone. I won't send you into that same mistake. Three sets of eyes are harder to silence than one, and harder to explain away if something goes wrong.
The warden is still holding the arena. Bring your two and go finish it.
You're back, and quiet about it. That's the badge, I take it. Hand it over.

Scored and cracked - his record, not yours. He taught more than adepts and specialists. There's an inner circle above him I need accounted for next, and I'd rather account for them before they notice their warden stopped answering.

Housecleaning. Four instructors left running what the warden built, and every one of them knew exactly what they were teaching. Bring me whichever of them is holding the captain's challenge chit when the other three are settled.
Go handle it. You've been quiet enough, long enough, that I'm not worried about the details.

The drill ledger told me who was being taught. The range relay told me how long it had been going on. The scored badge told me the warden knew it was unauthorized and ran it anyway. Bring me the chit, and I'll know exactly how deep this goes and who signed off on it.
They've sealed the floor above the arena, command space by the look of it. Same key opens that lock too. Whoever set this up never planned on someone getting this far in.
Four of them, and none of them used to working outnumbered. Bring the company you brought last time. I'd rather you finish this with witnesses than alone with a story I have to take on faith.
Four of the inner circle are still unaccounted for. Go account for them.
That's the chit. Let's see exactly how far this went.
Signatures, authorizations, all of it improvised after the fact to look official. This runs all the way to whoever taught the warden in the first place. One name left on the list.

The master is the source. Everything the warden taught, everything the inner circle covered for, traces back to him. I work alone because I trust exactly one person with my own exposure - myself. I'm not extending you the same rule. Bring people you'd trust with a secret that could end you, because that's what this is. When he's down, that's the last transmission this operation ever sends.
Then go end it. Quietly, if you can manage it. Permanently, either way.

I work alone because one person is easy to account for, easy to disappear if something goes wrong. You're not disposable the same way, and this isn't a job that forgives one mistake. Bring company. Let someone else carry half the risk of what happens down there.
The deepest floor of the annex, the one even the inner circle kept sealed from their own people. Your key still works. It was never really about the lock. It was about who had the nerve to use it.

He taught shutdown work before the warden ever learned to spell it. Nobody who went in alone came back to file a report. Bring people who know how to stay quiet about what they see, because they will see something.
The master is still down there, still unaccounted for. Go close the file.
You're back, and there's no report to write about him anymore. That's the confirmation I needed.

End of transmission. Nothing on record, nothing to investigate, no loose thread back to the annex. That's the job done the way it should always be done. Systemic Shutdown is yours; use it exactly as quietly as I taught you to.
Back to the ledger.
I'll take the first job.
What exactly is a shutdown strike?
Where do I find the annex?
What should I expect from the adepts?
Not yet.
Here's the drill ledger.
Back to the relay.
I'll take the second job.
Why keep this quiet at all?
Where are the specialists working?
What should I expect this time?
Give me time to think it through.
Here's the range relay.
Back to the badge.
I'll bring the company and go.
Who taught the students this in the first place?
Where's the warden's floor?
What should I know about him?
I need to find the right two first.
Here's the badge.
Back to the chit.
I'll clean house.
What do the recovered items tell you?
Where's the inner circle hiding?
What am I walking into?
Let me finish arranging things.
Here's the chit.
Back to it.
I'll bring people I trust. Let's close this out.
Why send me with company when you work alone?
Where do I find him?
What should I expect from the master?
I need to be sure of who's coming with me.
It's done. He's off the books for good.
